title: World War III Imminent | L. Kasradze & A. Kachikian
summary: Two Caucasus analysts call the Iran war an attack on Russia and China, warn of an oil shock and a 1914-style spread, while one argues nuclear deterrence will keep the great powers from fighting.

assertions.quote: the prices for fuel, gas, oil and then food prices are going to skyrocket. We're facing a global economic crisis.

It is a World War III but it is peripheral because the big powers can't fight directly.
if you look at the big picture, this is an attack on on Russia and China.

verdicts.note: The paper gives the war's aims as subduing Iran or toppling its regime and does not mention weakening Russia or China.

assertions.quote: the three countries will basically stabilize the situation realizing fully that they cannot kill each other because they're all nuclear powers.

you can't change a regime without ground troops.

verdicts.note: The air campaign failed to topple the regime and the US weighed a limited ground operation on Kharg Island, but the paper does not show that ground troops would succeed.
